84307.sol: The passage of end products of digestion through the mucosal lining of alimentary canal into blood and lymph is called absorption. 84424.sol: The plasma fluid that filters out from glomerular capillaries into Bowman's capsule of nephron is called glomerular filtrate. A comparison of the volume of the filtrate formed per day (180 ~L / day) with that of the urine released (1.5 ~L ) , suggests that nearly 99 per cent of the filtrate has to be reabsorbed by the renal tubules. This process is called reabsorption.

124013.subject: Botany
124013.text: What is the name of the network of tiny tubular structures found in eukaryotic cells?
124013.sol: Electron microscopic studies of eukaryotic cells reveal the presence of a network or reticulum of tiny tubular structures scattered in the cytoplasm that is called the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) . Hence, ER divides the intracellular space into two distinct compartments, i.e., luminal (inside ER) and extra luminal (cytoplasm) compartments.

124220.subject: Botany
124220.text: Membrane Model Features Characteristics A. Lipid bilayer 1. Provides membrane stability B. Proteins 2. Allows protein movement C. Cholesterol 3. Major structural component D. Fluidity 4. Interacts with lipids and proteins
124220.sol: The lipid bilayer is the major structural component of the membrane.Proteins interact with lipids and contribute to membrane fluidity.Cholesterol provides stability to the membrane.Fluidity allows for the lateral movement of proteins within the membrane.

124300.subject: Botany
124300.text: Which of the following pairs of a cellular structure and its corresponding cell part or organelle is incorrectly matched?
124300.sol: Thylakoids are flattened membranous sacs present in the stroma of plastids (chloroplasts). The tonoplast is the single membrane that bounds the central vacuole in plant cells. Kinetochores are disc-shaped structures present on the sides of the centromere in chromosomes. Cristae are the infoldings of the inner membrane of mitochondria. The Golgi apparatus, on the other hand, consists of flat, disc-shaped sacs called cisternae. Therefore, the pair 'Cristae - Golgi apparatus' is incorrectly matched. Answer: Cristae -

124468.subject: Botany
124468.text: Cell theory was propounded in 1838-39 by :
124468.sol: The cell theory or cell doctrine is credited to Matthias Schleiden (1838) a botanist of Germany and Theodor Schwann (1839), a zoologist also of Germany.

124564.subject: Botany
124564.text: Where is the application of decapitation widely used?
124564.sol: Removal of shoot tips (decapitation) usually results in the growth of lateral buds. It is widely applied in tea plantations, hedge-making. Auxins also induce parthenocarpy, e.g., in tomatoes. They are widely used as herbicides. 2, 4-D, widely used to kill dicotyledonous weeds, does not affect mature monocotyledonous plants. It is used to prepare weed-free lawns by gardeners.

125216.subject: Botany
125216.text: In respiration from 180 ~g of glucose which of the following is formed?
options: 264gm CO C ₂+190 gm H ₂ O +391 Kcal
264 gm CO +108 gm H H ₂ O +686 Kcal
390 gm CO +108 gm H H ₂ O +686 Kcal
390 gm CO ₂+264 gm H ₂ O +391 Kcal
125216.sol: In respiration, from 180 gm of glucose 264 gm CO CO ₂+108 gm H ₂ O +686 Kcal energy is formed. 125300.subject: Botany
125300.text: What transformation is involved in photosynthesis?
125300.sol: All animals including human beings depend on plants for their food. Have you ever wondered from where plants get their food? Green plants, in fact, have to make or rather synthesise the food they need and all other organisms depend on them for their needs. The green plants make or rather synthesise the food they need through photosynthesis and are therefore called autotrophs. You have already learnt that the autotrophic nutrition is found only in plants and all other organisms that depend on the green plants for fo

125323.subject: Botany
125323.text: The action spectrum of photosynthesis roughly resembles the absorption spectra of which pigments?
125323.sol: Now consider the interesting experiments done by T.W Engelmann (1843 – 1909). Using a prism he split light into its spectral components and then illuminated a green alga, Cladophora, placed in a suspension of aerobic bacteria. The bacteria were used to detect the sites of O2 evolution. He observed that the bacteria accumulated mainly in the region of blue and red light of the split spectrum. A first action spectrum of photosynthesis was thus described. It resembles roughly the absorption spectra of chlorophyll a an

125442.subject: Botany
125442.text: What type of leaf anatomy do C4 plants have?
125442.sol: The particularly large cells around the vascular bundles of the C4 plants are called bundle sheath cells, and the leaves which have such anatomy are said to have ‘Kranz’ anatomy. ‘Kranz’ means ‘wreath’ and is a reflection of the arrangement of cells. The bundle sheath cells may form several layers around the vascular bundles; they are characterised by having a large number of chloroplasts, thick walls impervious to gaseous exchange and no intercellular spaces. You may like to cut a section of the leaves of C4 plant

125572.subject: Botany
125572.text: Read the following statements and choose the following option: 1. There are three photosystem 2. Water stress decreases the surface area of leaves 3. Photosynthesis is the secondary source of all food on earth 4. Jan ingenhousz discovered oxygen in 1774. 5. The O2 released is from water; this was proved using radio isobar techniques
125572.sol: Water stress makes leaves wilt, thus, reducing the surface area of the leaves and their metabolic activity as well.

125676.subject: Botany
125676.text: A researcher adds a chemical agent to an isolated chloroplast suspension that makes the thylakoid membrane highly permeable to protons. If this suspension is exposed to light, which of the following processes will be immediately inhibited?
options: Absorption of light energy by photosystems
125676.sol: According to the chemiosmotic hypothesis, the synthesis of ATP is strictly dependent on the creation and maintenance of a proton gradient across the thylakoid membrane. If a chemical agent makes the membrane highly permeable to protons, the protons will simply diffuse back into the stroma without passing through the ATP synthase enzyme ( CF₀ - CF₁ complex). Consequently, no proton gradient can be established, and ATP synthesis will be immediately inhibited. The absorption of light, splitting of water, and electron

125911.subject: Botany
125911.text: What is the effect of having both male and female flowers on the same plant, such as in castor and maize?
options: It prevents autogamy but not geitonogamy
It prevents both autogamy and geitonogamy
It synchronizes pollen release and stigma receptivity
125911.sol: Outbreeding Devices: Majority of flowering plants produce hermaphrodite flowers and pollen grains are likely to come in contact with the stigma of the same flower. Both these devices prevent autogamy. The third device to prevent inbreeding is self-incompatibility. This is a genetic mechanism and prevents self-pollen (from the same flower or other flowers of the same plant) from fertilising the ovules by inhibiting pollen germination or pollen tube growth in the pistil. Another device to prevent self-pollination is

126187.subject: Botany
126187.text: The process of seed formation without the occurrence of Fertilisation is called ____
126187.sol: The process of seed formation without the occurrence of Fertilisation is called apomixis

126276.subject: Botany
126276.text: In a typical angiosperm, if the chromosome number in the endosperm is 72 , what will be the chromosome number in its synergid cell and secondary nucleus, respectively?
126276.sol: The endosperm of a typical angiosperm is a triploid ( 3n ) tissue formed by triple fusion. Given the endosperm chromosome number is 72 , we have 3n = 72 , which means the haploid chromosome number is n = 24 . The synergid is a cell of the female gametophyte (embryo sac) and is haploid ( n ). Therefore, its chromosome number is 24 . The secondary nucleus is formed by the fusion of two haploid polar nuclei in the central cell before fertilization, making it diploid ( 2n ). Therefore, its chromosome number is 2 24 = 4

126309.subject: Botany
126309.text: Assertion : Colpa aurea is a specialised pollinating agent of orchid Ophrys speculum. Reason : Male Colpa mistakes the Ophrys flower for female wasp to copulate with it.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
126309.sol: For its pollination, the orchid Ophrys speculum has picked the most selective attraction in the entire animal kingdom. It is pollinated by a hairy wasp, Colpa aurea. The wasp has a fixed habit whereby its males leave the burrows for above ground existence about four weeks before the females emerge for the open air mating. The orchid opens its flowers about the same time the males appear and they possess an appearance and odour similar to those possessed by the female wasp. The inexperienced males mistake the Ophrys

126480.subject: Botany
126480.text: What type of bond links amino acids in a polypeptide or a protein?
126480.sol: In a polypeptide or a protein, amino acids are linked by a peptide bond , which is formed when the carboxyl (-COOH) group of one amino acid reacts with the amino (-NH₂) group of the next amino acid with the elimination of a water moiety.

126801.subject: Botany
126801.text: Lecithin, a small molecular weight organic compound found in living tissues, is an example of:
126801.sol: The correct answer is option (1). Some lipids have phosphorous and a phosphorylated organic compound in them. These are phospholipids. They are found in cell membrane. Lecithin is one example. Option (2) is incorrect as glycerides are another group of lipids in which both glycerol and fatty acids are present. Option (3) and (4) are incorrect as amino acids and carbohydrates are separate groups of biomolecules.

126857.subject: Botany
126857.text: Which one of the following biomolecules is correctly characterised?
options: Lecithin-A phosphorylated glyceride found in cell membrane
Palmitic acid-An unsaturated fatty acid with 18 carbon atoms
Adenylic acid-Adenosine with a glucose phosphate molecule
Alanine amino acid-Contains an amino group and an acidic group anywhere in the molecule
126857.sol: Alanine is a neutral amino acid with non-cyclic hydrocarbon chain, one amino group and one carboxyl group. Palmitic acid is saturated fatty acid adenylic acid has pentose sugar in it not glucose.

127247.subject: Botany
options: Protecting endangered species in their natural habitat
Protective maintenance in zoological parks and botanical gardens
127247.sol: Biodiversity conservation may be in situ as well as ex situ . In in situ conservation, the endangered species are protected in their natural habitat so that the entire ecosystem is protected. Recently, 34 ‘biodiversity hotspots’ in the world have been proposed for intensive conservation efforts. Of these, three (Western Ghats-Sri Lanka, Himalaya and Indo-Burma) cover India’s rich biodiversity regions. Our country’s in situ conservation efforts are reflected in its 14 biosphere reserves, 90 national parks, > 450 wil

127352.subject: Botany
127352.text: Which of the following is not a cause for loss of biodiversity?
127352.sol: Destruction of habitat, invasion by alien species, and over-exploitation, of natural resources are cause for loss of biodiversity.

127384.subject: Botany
127384.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): It is economically feasible and realistic for all nations to conserve all their biological wealth in situ . Reason (R): The number of species waiting to be saved from extinction far exceeds the conservation resources available due to the conflict between development and conservation. In the light o
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
127384.sol: According to NCERT, faced with the conflict between development and conservation, many nations find it unrealistic and economically not feasible to conserve all their biological wealth. Therefore, Assertion (A) is false. Invariably, the number of species waiting to be saved from extinction far exceeds the conservation resources available. This makes Reason (R) a true statement. Hence, (A) is false but (R) is true. Answer: (A) is false but (R) is true

127386.subject: Botany
127386.text: When a large, contiguous forest is broken up into smaller, isolated patches due to human activities, the populations of certain species decline drastically. According to ecological principles, which of the following groups of animals is most adversely affected by this habitat fragmentation?
options: Mammals and birds requiring large territories and animals with migratory habits
Small rodents and insects that have high reproductive rates and small territories
Species that thrive in edge habitats and have broad environmental tolerances
Organisms that occupy highly specialized, non-migratory local niches within a single patch
127386.sol: According to NCERT, habitat fragmentation is a major cause of biodiversity loss. When large habitats are broken up into small fragments due to various human activities, mammals and birds requiring large territories and certain animals with migratory habits are badly affected, leading to population declines. Species with small territories or those that thrive in edge habitats are generally less affected or may even increase in number. Highly specialized non-migratory organisms might be affected by habitat loss, but

127940.subject: Zoology
127940.text: What does the lymphatic system in frogs consist of?
options: Lymph, lymph channels, and lymph nodes
127940.sol: The vascular system of frog is well-developed closed type. Frogs have a lymphatic system also. The blood vascular system involves heart, blood vessels and blood. The lymphatic system consists of lymph, lymph channels and lymph nodes. Heart is a muscular structure situated in the upper part of the body cavity. It has three chambers, two atria and one ventricle and is covered by a membrane called pericardium. A triangular structure called sinus venosus joins the right atrium. It receives blood through the major veins

128025.subject: Zoology
128025.text: Select the correct statement from the ones given below with respect to Periplaneta americana
options: Grinding of food is carried out only by the mouth parts
Nervous system located dorsally, consists of segmentally arranged ganglia joined by a pair of longitudinal con
Males bear a pair of short thread like anal styles
There are 16 very long Malpighian tubules present at the junctions of midgut and hindgut
128025.sol: The abdomen in both males and females consists of 10 segments. In females, the 7th sternum is boat shaped and together with the 8th and 9th sterna forms a brood or genital pouch whose anterior part contains female gonopore, spermathecal pores and collateral glands. In males, genital pouch or chamber lies at the hind end of the abdomen bounded dorsally by 9th and 10th terga and ventrally by the 9th sternum. It contains dorsal anus, ventral male genital pore and gonapophysis. Males bear a pair of short, thread- like

128409.subject: Zoology
128409.text: Select the correct statement with respect to the following figure.
options: The hypothalamus is located in a bony cavity called sella tursica.
Pituitary is divided anatomically into an adenohypophysis and a neurohypophysis.
Pars intermedia is almost merged with pars distalis.
Posterior pituitary, stores and releases two hormones called oxytocin and vasopressin.
128409.sol: The pituitary gland is located in a bony cavity called sella tursica and is attached to the hypothalamus by a stalk (Figure 22.2). It is divided anatomically into an adenohypophysis and a neurohypophysis. Adenohypophysis consists of two portions, pars distalis and pars intermedia.

128496.subject: Zoology
128496.text: Read the following statements and choose the correct option: 1. The releasing hormones are hormones which stimulate secretion of pituitary hormones and the inhibiting hormones are hormones which inhibit secretions of pituitary hormones 2. A hypothalamic hormone called Gonadotrophin releasing hormone (GnRH) stimulates the pituitary synthesis and release of gonadotrophins 3. Somatostatin from the hypothalamus inhibits
128496.sol: The releasing hormones are hormones which stimulate secretion of pituitary hormones and the inhibiting hormones are hormones which inhibit secretions of pituitary hormones. A hypothalamic hormone called Gonadotrophin releasing hormone (GnRH) stimulates the pituitary synthesis and release of gonadotrophins. Somatostatin from the hypothalamus inhibits the release of growth hormone from the pituitary

128528.subject: Zoology
128528.text: Read the following statements and choose the correct option: 1. Gastrin acts on the gastric glands and stimulates the secretion of hydrochloric acid and pepsinogen 2. Secretin inhibits gastric secretion and motility 3. CCK acts on both pancreas and gall bladder and stimulates the secretion of pancreatic enzymes and bile juice, respectively 4. GIP acts on the exocrine pancreas and stimulates secretion of water and bic
128528.sol: Gastrin acts on the gastric glands and stimulates the secretion of hydrochloric acid and pepsinogen. GIP inhibits gastric secretion and motility. CCK acts on both pancreas and gall bladder and stimulates the secretion of pancreatic enzymes and bile juice, respectively. Secretin acts on the exocrine pancreas and stimulates secretion of water and bicarbonate ions

128584.subject: Zoology
128584.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): Secretion of Atrial Natriuretic Factor (ANF) causes a decrease in blood pressure. Reason (R): ANF is a peptide hormone that causes constriction of the blood vessels. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
128584.sol: Assertion (A) is true: The atrial wall of our heart secretes a peptide hormone called Atrial Natriuretic Factor (ANF) in response to increased blood pressure, and its primary function is to decrease blood pressure. Reason (R) is false: ANF decreases blood pressure by causing dilation (widening) of the blood vessels, not constriction. Vasoconstriction would increase blood pressure, which is the opposite of ANF's function. Therefore, (A) is true but (R) is false. Answer: (A) is true but (R) is false

128607.subject: Zoology
128607.text: Which of the following is an incorrect statement regarding the physiological and metabolic effects of catecholamines secreted by the adrenal medulla?
options: They stimulate the breakdown of lipids.
They increase the rate of respiration and heartbeat.
They promote the synthesis of proteins from amino acids.
They stimulate the breakdown of glycogen resulting in hyperglycemia.
128607.sol: Adrenal medullary hormones (adrenaline and noradrenaline) are emergency hormones that prepare the body for fight or flight. Metabolically, they stimulate the breakdown of glycogen (glycogenolysis) resulting in an increased concentration of glucose in the blood (hyperglycemia). In addition, they also stimulate the breakdown of lipids (lipolysis) and proteins (proteolysis) to provide immediate energy. They do not promote the synthesis of proteins. Therefore, the statement claiming they promote protein synthesis is in

128780.subject: Zoology
128780.text: What are the formed elements in the blood called collectively?
128780.sol: Erythrocytes, leucocytes and platelets are collectively called formed elements and they constitute nearly 45 per cent of the blood.

128794.subject: Zoology
128794.text: What is the average life span of RBCs in the human body?
128794.sol: RBCs are devoid of nucleus in most of the mammals and are biconcave in shape. They have a red coloured, iron containing complex protein called haemoglobin, hence the colour and name of these cells. A healthy individual has 12-16 gms of haemoglobin in every 100 ml of blood. These molecules play a significant role in transport of respiratory gases . RBCs have an average life span of 120 days after which they are destroyed in the spleen (graveyard of RBCs).

128874.subject: Zoology
128874.text: What is the state of all four chambers of the heart during diastole?
128874.sol: Four chambers of heart are in a relaxed state, i.e., they are in joint diastole. As the tricuspid and bicuspid valves are open, blood from the pulmonary veins and vena cava flows into the left and the right ventricle respectively through the left and right atria. The semilunar valves are closed at this stage. The SAN now generates an action potential which stimulates both the atria to undergo a simultaneous contraction – the atrial systole. This increases the flow of blood into the ventricles by about 30 per cent.

129054.subject: Zoology
129054.text: Which of the following statements regarding secondary lymphoid organs is incorrect?
options: Peyer's patches of the large intestine act as secondary lymphoid organs.
Secondary lymphoid organs provide the sites for interaction of lymphocytes with the antigen.
After interaction with antigens, lymphocytes proliferate to become effector cells.
Lymph nodes serve to trap the micro-organisms which happen to get into the lymph and tissue fluid.
129054.sol: Peyer's patches are located in the small intestine, not the large intestine. Therefore, the statement identifying them as part of the large intestine is incorrect. Secondary lymphoid organs (such as the spleen, lymph nodes, tonsils, Peyer's patches of small intestine and appendix) provide the sites for interaction of lymphocytes with the antigen, which then proliferate to become effector cells. Lymph nodes are small solid structures located at different points along the lymphatic system that serve to trap the micro

129092.subject: Zoology
options: The process of filtration of urea in kidney
A type of locomotion found in Hydra
Migration of WBCs into the tissue spaces from blood capillaries
129092.sol: Diapedesis is the migration of blood cells through the walls of blood capillaries into tissues spaces. Diapedesis is an important part of the reaction of tissues to injury.

129746.subject: Zoology
129746.text: Assertion : While on going down the loop of Henle, the filtrate becomes hypotonic. Reason : The descending limb of loop of Henle is impermeable to both water and electrolytes.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false.
129746.sol: The descending limb of loop of Henle is permeable to water but almost impermeable to electrolytes. This concentrates the filtrate as it moves down.

129869.subject: Zoology
129869.text: What is the binding of oxygen with haemoglobin primarily related to?
129869.sol: Haemoglobin is a red coloured iron containing pigment present in the RBCs. O2 can bind with haemoglobin in a reversible manner to form oxyhaemoglobin. Each haemoglobin molecule can carry a maximum of four molecules of O2 . Binding of oxygen with haemoglobin is primarily related to partial pressure of O2. Partial pressure of CO2, hydrogen ion concentration and temperature are the other factors which can interfere with this binding. A sigmoid curve is obtained when percentage saturation of haemoglobin with O2 is plot

130279.subject: Zoology
130279.text: What type of immovable or slightly movable joint is a point of contact between bones?
130279.sol: .The human body consists of 206 bones in total. These bones are grouped into two main divisions - the axial skeleton and the appendicular skeleton. The skull is composed of two sets of bones, cranial and facial, that total to 22 bones.Each vertebra has a central hollow portion (neural canal) through which the spinal cord passes. The vertebral column is differentiated into cervical (7), thoracic (12), lumbar (5), sacral (1-fused) and coccygeal (1-fused) regions.Joints are essential for all types of movements involvi

130410.subject: Zoology
130410.text: Classification of Joints Description A. Fibrous Joint 1. Bones are connected by dense connective tissue; no movement B. Cartilaginous Joint 2. Bones are connected by cartilage; limited movement C. Synovial Joint 3. Allows sliding or gliding movements between bones D. Gliding Joint 4. Bones are separated by a fluid-filled joint cavity; free movement
130410.sol: Fibrous Joint: Bones are connected by dense connective tissue, allowing no or very little movement (e.g., sutures in the skull). Cartilaginous Joint: Bones are connected by cartilage, allowing limited movement (e.g., intervertebral discs). Synovial Joint: Bones are separated by a fluid-filled joint cavity, allowing free movement (e.g., knee joint). Gliding Joint: Allows sliding or gliding movements between flat bone surfaces (e.g., joints between the carpals).

130550.subject: Zoology
130550.text: What aspect of Reproductive Health care does the implementation of better techniques and new strategies aim to improve?
130550.sol: Successful implementation of various action plans to attain Reproductive Health requires strong infrastructural facilities, professional expertise and material support. These are essential to provide medical assistance and care to people in reproduction-related problems like pregnancy, delivery, STDs, abortions, contraception, menstrual problems, infertility, etc. Implementation of better techniques and new strategies from time to time are also required to provide more efficient care and assistance to people. Statu

130551.subject: Zoology
130551.text: What is the primary goal of the statutory ban on amniocentesis for sex determination?
options: To legally check increasing female foeticides
130551.sol: Successful implementation of various action plans to attain Reproductive Health requires strong infrastructural facilities, professional expertise and material support. These are essential to provide medical assistance and care to people in reproduction-related problems like pregnancy, delivery, STDs, abortions, contraception, menstrual problems, infertility, etc. Implementation of better techniques and new strategies from time to time are also required to provide more efficient care and assistance to people. Statu

130586.subject: Zoology
130586.text: For what situations are emergency contraceptives particularly useful?
options: Avoiding possible pregnancy due to rape or casual unprotected intercourse
130586.sol: Progestogens alone or in combination with estrogen can also be used by females as injections or implants under the skin . Their mode of action is similar to that of pills and their effective periods are much longer. Administration of progestogens or progestogen-estrogen combinations or IUDs within 72 hours of coitus have been found to be very effective as emergency contraceptives as they could be used to avoid possible pregnancy due to rape or casual unprotected intercourse.

130895.subject: Zoology
130895.text: How many gamete mother cells are formed in each fetal ovary during embryonic development?
130895.sol: The process of formation of a mature female gamete is called oogenesis which is markedly different from spermatogenesis. Oogenesis is initiated during the embryonic development stage when a couple of million gamete mother cells (oogonia ) are formed within each fetal ovary; no more oogonia are formed and added after birth. These cells start division and enter into prophase-I of the meiotic division and get temporarily arrested at that stage, called primary oocytes. Each primary oocyte then gets surrounded by a laye

131062.subject: Zoology
131062.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: The blastocyst becomes embedded in the myometrium of the uterus. Reason: Only fertilisation leads to Pregnancy.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
131062.sol: The blastocyst becomes embedded in the endometrium of the uterus. Implantation leads to Pregnancy.

131228.subject: Zoology
131228.text: Match List-I with List-II regarding the phases of the menstrual cycle and their corresponding hormonal profiles. List-I List-II A. Follicular phase I. LH surge B. Ovulatory phase II. Peak progesterone with low FSH and LH C. Luteal phase III. Gradual increase in FSH and rising estrogen Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
131228.sol: During the follicular phase (A), the secretion of gonadotropins (FSH and LH) increases gradually. This stimulates follicular development as well as the secretion of estrogens by the growing follicles (III). During the ovulatory phase (B), the rapid secretion of LH leads to its maximum level during the mid-cycle. This is called the LH surge (I), which induces the rupture of the Graafian follicle and thereby the release of the ovum. During the luteal phase (C), the remaining parts of the ruptured follicle transform i

131676.subject: Zoology
131676.text: Select the correct statement for the given figure.
options: Francis Crick proposed the Central dogma in molecular biology.
Francis Crick proposed the Central dogma which states that the genetic information flows from DNA to RNA to Pr
In some viruses the flow of information is in reverse direction, that is, from RNA to DNA.

Very soon, Francis Crick proposed the Central dogma in molecular biology, which states that the genetic information flows from DNA→RNA→Protein.In some viruses the flow of information is in reverse direction, that is, from RNA to DNA.

132161.subject: Zoology
132161.text: What was the genotype of the F1 hybrid in Mendel's dihybrid cross?
132161.sol: The genotype of the parents can then be written as RRYY and rryy. The cross between the two plants can be written down as in Figure 4.7 showing the genotypes of the parent plants. The gametes RY and ry unite on fertilization to produce the F1 hybrid RrYy . When Mendel self hybridized the F1 plants he found that 3/4th of F2 plants had yellow seeds and 1/4th had green. The yellow and green colour segregated in a 3:1 ratio. Round and wrinkled seed shape also segregated in a 3:1 ratio; just like in a monohybrid cross.

132409.subject: Zoology
132409.text: A diploid organism is heterozygous for 4 loci, how many types of gametes can be produced?
132409.sol: If an entity is heterozygous at four loci with four different characters, then while meiotic division, they split to form 8 different gametes.

132645.subject: Zoology
132645.text: A man of blood group 'A', marries a woman of blood group 'B', both of them are heterozygous for blood group, chances of their first child having blood group AB will be
132645.sol: Man Blood group Women Blood group There is 25 % chances of first offspring having blood group AB.

132819.subject: Zoology
132819.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: The beak shapes of Darwin’s finches are a result of natural selection. Reason: Different beak shapes evolved to exploit different food resources on the Galapagos Islands.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
132819.sol: the beak shapes of Darwin’s finches evolved to suit different food resources, providing a classic example of natural selection.

133398.subject: Zoology
133398.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: HIV enters macrophages and uses reverse transcriptase to convert its RNA genome into viral DNA. Reason: The viral DNA integrates into the host cell's DNA, directing the production of new virus particles.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
133398.sol: The word AIDS stands for Acquired Immuno Deficiency Syndrome. This means deficiency of immune system, acquired during the lifetime of an individual indicating that it is not a congenital disease. ‘Syndrome’ means a group of symptoms. AIDS was first reported in 1981 and in the last twenty-five years or so, it has spread all over the world killing more than 25 million persons. 95926.subject: Botany
95926.sol: Plastids a double membrane organelles responsible for manufacturing and storing food in plant cells and few other eukaryotic organisms. They are not found in prokaryotes like bacteria and blue-green algae and fungi which are heterotrophic eukaryotes.

96494.subject: Botany

96494.sol: Biotic and abiotic components interact and form a physical structure which is unique for each type of ecosystem. For example, trees occupy top layer of a forest, smaller plants the second and weeds and grasses occupy the bottom layers. Pyramid of numbers provide information regarding the relationship between organisms at each trophic level in a ecosystem.

306569.sol: At the geomagnetic poles, the Earth's magnetic field is entirely vertical. The horizontal component of the Earth's magnetic field, B_ H , is zero at the magnetic poles.
